questions.q: What does Bernstein say about so-called idle thoughts?
a: They don't exist, because every thought sends out energy
They are harmless unless you act on them
They are the main source of everyday anxiety
They should always be replaced with affirmations
questions.why: Lesson 1 draws on A Course in Miracles to argue that every single thought has a positive or negative effect.

questions.q: What are the three steps of Bernstein's Choose Again method?
a: Notice your feelings, thank your thoughts, then ask for happier ones
Breathe deeply, count to ten, then respond calmly
Write the fear down, burn it, then set a new goal
Picture success, repeat a mantra, then take action
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes recognizing thought patterns, expressing gratitude for them and then choosing again.

questions.q: What is the first step of the 'think it to feel it' practice?
a: Recall a past experience that gave you the feeling you want
Say a mantra aloud until you believe it
Write down what you want a year from now
Ask a friend to describe how you seem to them
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to remember an event that produced the emotion you want to feel again, then declare it.

questions.q: How does Bernstein's friend Alex get past a bad business decision?
a: He starts appreciating what the experience taught him
He hires a coach to rebuild his confidence
He takes a long break away from work
He asks his partners to forgive him
questions.why: Lesson 3 says gratitude for what he learned let Alex see a way forward and leave the negativity behind.

questions.q: How does Bernstein find gratitude when her children track dirt into the house?
a: She treats the mess as proof that she gets to have kids
She reminds herself that the mess will pass quickly
She asks her children to clean it up themselves
She compares it with problems other people face
questions.why: Lesson 3 says she looks for the hidden benefit in a frustrating situation.
